subject: Are there constraints on factor levels names in INLA?

messages.author: 40cb5026d0e9f97c
messages.subject: Are there constraints on factor levels names in INLA?
parts:
I get INLA to crash on a simple logistic regression y~x with 3017 obs.
Renaming the levels of the factor x  into a,b,c,d,e "solves" the problem.

Are there constraints on factor levels names in INLA? Am I missing a deeper problem here? 

dat = read.table('http://www2.imm.dtu.dk/~gigu/share/crash-report.txt')
str(dat)
levels(dat$x)

# inla-program exited with an error
m1.inla = inla(data=dat,
               formula = y~x,
               family = 'binomial',
               Ntrials = rep(nrow(dat),1),
               verbose=TRUE)

# "solving" problem
levels(dat$x) = letters[1:5]
m1.inla = inla(data=dat,
               formula = y~x,
               family = 'binomial',
               Ntrials = rep(nrow(dat),1),
               verbose=TRUE)
summary(m1.inla)

Thx, 
Gilles

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Are there constraints on factor levels names in INLA?
parts:
yes, having '[]' in the names will not work, as the model file will
give section names like


[x]1-1.5]]
dir = fixed.effect00000002
type = linear
covariates = $inladatadir/file3b024bc0c686
compute = 1
mean = 0
precision = 0.001

[x]1.5-3]]
dir = fixed.effect00000003
type = linear
covariates = $inladatadir/file3b0220552286
compute = 1

and then its just a mess... as its reads the names inside '[NAME]'

I agree, there should be an error given in this case.

H
